quests.instruction: Your family surprises you with the one gift you have dreamed about for years. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about years of dreaming coming true all at once.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than delighted — ecstatic fits years of dreaming coming true at once, a much bigger joy than one delightful moment.
quests.funFact: A wish coming true after years of waiting often feels even bigger because of how long you dreamed about it!

quests.instruction: Your sibling deliberately ruins the surprise you had been planning for weeks. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of angry — think about weeks of careful planning undone on purpose.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than disappointed — furious fits weeks of careful planning being deliberately undone.
quests.funFact: Even a ruined surprise can sometimes be turned into a fun new plan with a little creativity!

quests.instruction: You are swimming and suddenly realize the water has gotten much deeper than you expected. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about a sudden realization that you are out of your depth.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than nervous — terrified fits the sudden realization of being out of your depth, a much bigger fear than the flutter before swimming begins.
quests.funFact: Swimming parallel to the shore and calling for a lifeguard is the safest response if this ever happens.

quests.instruction: You just finished building an enormous block castle completely on your own, and it did not fall down once. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about looking back at something you just finished, not about how sure you feel going into the next task.
quests.explanation: This is proud rather than confident — proud looks back at something you just accomplished, while confident looks forward to trusting your own skill next time.
quests.funFact: Finishing something difficult is one of the best ways to earn this warm, accomplished feeling!

quests.instruction: You have been looking forward to a sleepover with your cousins for the entire month. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about a bouncy readiness for something you know is coming very soon, stronger and more specific than a general wish.
quests.explanation: This is eager rather than hopeful — eager fits a bouncy readiness for something you know is coming soon, while hopeful is a lighter wish without a set plan.
quests.funFact: Counting down the days on a calendar is a fun way to enjoy this bouncy, ready feeling!

quests.instruction: You are the only one in your group who has never been camping before, and everyone else is sharing camping stories. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about doubting yourself because you lack an experience others share, not about being in an unfamiliar social situation.
quests.explanation: This is insecure rather than shy — insecure comes from doubting yourself next to others' experience, while shy comes from an unfamiliar social situation itself.
quests.funFact: Everyone has their own list of firsts still to come — camping might just be one of yours!

quests.instruction: Your handmade birdhouse finally attracts its very first family of birds after weeks of waiting. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a bright burst of joy about something wonderful finally happening, not simply a worry ending.
quests.explanation: This is delighted rather than relieved — delighted is a bright burst of joy about something wonderful happening, while relieved is more about a worry finally ending.
quests.funFact: Birds often choose birdhouses that feel safe and quiet — yours must be just right!

quests.instruction: You finish reading the very last page of a book series you have loved for years. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a quiet, satisfied feeling about a wonderful ending, not a letdown or sorrow.
quests.explanation: This is content rather than sad — content is the quiet satisfaction of a wonderful ending, even though saying goodbye to a beloved story can feel bittersweet.
quests.funFact: Rereading a favorite series is a wonderful way to enjoy the story all over again!

quests.instruction: You have practiced your violin every day for a month and can now play the whole song perfectly. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about feeling sure you can do it again, not about looking back at what you already achieved.
quests.explanation: This is confident rather than proud — confident looks ahead, trusting you can do it again, while proud looks back at what you have already achieved.
quests.funFact: This sure, ready feeling usually comes from exactly this kind of steady daily practice!

quests.instruction: Your grandmother, who lives far away, calls just to say she is thinking about you. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about appreciating someone's kindness, not about missing them.
quests.explanation: This is thankful rather than homesick — thankful is about appreciating someone's kindness, while homesick is about missing a familiar place or person.
quests.funFact: Calling back to say thank you is a lovely way to share this warm, grateful feeling!

quests.instruction: Your bike has a flat tire the morning of the race you have been training for. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about an unlucky problem getting in your way, not simply missing out on something.
quests.explanation: This is frustrated rather than disappointed — frustrated fits an unlucky problem blocking your plans, while disappointed usually follows simply missing out on something you wanted.
quests.funFact: Checking your bike the night before a big race is a smart habit that can help avoid this exact problem!

quests.instruction: You will not stop talking about the fascinating documentary about outer space you watched last night. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about overflowing excitement to share something, not the urge to investigate something unknown.
quests.explanation: This is enthusiastic rather than curious — enthusiastic is the overflowing excitement to share something you loved, while curious is the urge to learn more about something unknown.
quests.funFact: This bursting excitement to share is a great sign you found something you truly love learning about!

quests.instruction: You keep thinking about your upcoming dentist appointment, even though it is still four days away. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a restless feeling that lingers over several days, not a short flutter right before something happens.
quests.explanation: This is anxious rather than nervous — anxious lingers over time before something happens, while nervous is the short, fluttery feeling right before it starts.
quests.funFact: Talking through what will actually happen at the appointment can help this lingering feeling settle.

quests.instruction: You are giving a class presentation, and you accidentally knock over your poster in front of everyone. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is the warm feeling right after an actual small mishap, not the fluttery feeling before it started.
quests.explanation: This is embarrassed rather than nervous — embarrassed follows an actual mishap that just happened, while nervous is the fluttery feeling that comes before something begins.
quests.funFact: A quick calm laugh and picking the poster back up is a great way to move past this moment!

quests.instruction: You watch an ant carry a crumb many times its own size across the sidewalk. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a wide-eyed feeling of astonishment at something incredible, stronger than simple curiosity.
quests.explanation: This is amazed rather than curious — amazed is a wide-eyed feeling of astonishment at something incredible, while curious is more about wanting to learn more.
quests.funFact: Ants can carry objects many times their own body weight — one of nature's tiniest superpowers!

quests.instruction: You are the last one to leave a fun birthday party because you are having such a wonderful time. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a big, bubbling happiness from a whole event, not a quiet satisfaction or a single delightful moment.
quests.explanation: This is joyful rather than delighted — joyful describes big, bubbling happiness across a whole fun event, while delighted usually describes one bright, specific moment.
quests.funFact: Parties full of laughter and games are a classic way this deep, bubbling happiness shows up!

quests.instruction: You spend the whole weekend inside because you are grounded for something small, while your friends are out having fun without you. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a heavy, low feeling from several things piling up together, more than simple boredom or missing company alone.
quests.explanation: This is miserable rather than bored — miserable is a heavier, low feeling from missing out and feeling stuck all at once, while bored is simply having nothing to do.
quests.funFact: A tough weekend like this always gives way to a completely fresh one the following week!

quests.instruction: You keep thinking about how your friend's project has way more detail and color than yours. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about wanting what someone else has, not about doubting your own general worth.
quests.explanation: This is envious rather than insecure — envious is about wanting what someone else's work has, while insecure is more about doubting your own worth in general.
quests.funFact: Looking at a friend's project can also spark fresh new ideas of your own!

quests.instruction: You carefully read the pool rules and check the depth markers before choosing where to swim. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about taking careful safety steps on purpose, not a fluttery or uneasy feeling.
quests.explanation: This is cautious rather than worried — cautious is about taking careful, purposeful safety steps, while worried is more of an uneasy feeling about what might happen.
quests.funFact: Checking depth markers before swimming is exactly the kind of careful habit that keeps swimmers safe!

quests.instruction: You finally find the shoe you have been searching the entire house for, right where you first looked. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about a worry ending, not about feeling silly for missing it the first time.
quests.explanation: This is relieved rather than embarrassed — relieved fits the worry ending once you find it, even if you also feel a little silly about missing it at first.
quests.funFact: Checking the same spot twice sometimes works because we do not always look closely the first time!

quests.instruction: You are on a long trip and keep picturing your own cozy bedroom back home. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about missing the familiar comfort of home specifically, not missing company in general or feeling worn out.
quests.explanation: This is homesick rather than lonely — homesick is about missing the familiar comfort of home specifically, while lonely is more about missing company in general.
quests.funFact: A favorite small item from home can help this longing feeling feel smaller during a long trip!

quests.instruction: You have been waiting three weeks to hear back about the puppy you hope to adopt. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a light, wishing feeling focused on good news to come, not a restless dread or a wish for things to hurry up.
quests.explanation: This is hopeful rather than anxious — hopeful is a light, wishing feeling focused on good news to come, while anxious is a heavier, more restless worry.
quests.funFact: Checking in politely with the shelter is a good way to stay connected while you hopefully wait!

quests.instruction: You notice a new kid standing alone at recess and you are not sure whether to go say hello. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is the quiet, unsure feeling of approaching someone new, not doubt about your own worth.
quests.explanation: This is shy rather than insecure — shy is the quiet, unsure feeling of approaching someone new, while insecure is more about doubting your own worth or skill.
quests.funFact: Saying a simple 'hi, want to play?' is a brave first step that often turns into a new friendship!

quests.instruction: You keep checking your grade on the class website every few minutes on the day report cards are posted. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about wanting news to arrive faster, not a lingering, restless dread over several days.
quests.explanation: This is impatient rather than anxious — impatient is about wanting news to arrive faster right now, while anxious is more of a lingering, restless feeling over time.
quests.funFact: Finding something else to do for a few minutes can help this eager, checking feeling pass faster!

quests.instruction: Your parents tell you that you are finally getting the puppy you have begged for for years. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger version of happy — think about years of hoping and asking finally paying off.
quests.explanation: This is ecstatic rather than happy — ecstatic fits years of hoping and asking finally paying off, a much bigger joy than everyday happiness.
quests.funFact: This joyful news is often the start of an even more joyful new friendship with a new puppy!

quests.instruction: Someone deliberately destroys the science project you spent three whole months building. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much bigger, hotter version of angry — think about losing months of work on purpose, not just a small unfair moment.
quests.explanation: This is furious rather than simply angry — furious is a much stronger, hotter version of angry, fitting a huge, deliberate loss like this.
quests.funFact: Taking several slow, deep breaths is an important first step to help even this strong feeling settle before reacting.

quests.instruction: The ground suddenly begins shaking during an earthquake. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is a much stronger version of scared — think about the ground itself feeling unsteady beneath you.
quests.explanation: This is terrified rather than scared — terrified fits the ground itself feeling unsteady, a much bigger fear than an everyday startle.
quests.funFact: Knowing to get under a sturdy table during an earthquake is a safety step many schools practice with drills.

quests.instruction: You are the one who suggested a plan, and it works out even better than everyone expected. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about feeling good over your own idea working out, not about being astonished by something surprising.
quests.explanation: This is proud rather than amazed — proud comes from your own idea working out well, while amazed is more about astonishment at something unexpected.
quests.funFact: Having your idea work out is one of the best ways to build confidence for your next big idea!

quests.instruction: Your class is asked who wants to be the very first to try the new science experiment, and your hand shoots straight up. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about wanting to jump in first, not about being sure of your own skill or talking excitedly about it afterward.
quests.explanation: This is eager rather than enthusiastic — eager is about wanting to jump in and go first, while enthusiastic is more about the excited, talkative energy after you get started.
quests.funFact: Volunteering to go first is a great sign of this bouncy, ready-to-try feeling!

quests.instruction: You are not sure if you should join the new after-school club because you do not know if you will fit in. How do you feel?
quests.hint: This is about doubting whether you belong, not about being careful for safety or feeling quiet around new people.
quests.explanation: This is insecure rather than cautious — insecure is about doubting whether you belong, while cautious is about being careful, usually for safety.
quests.funFact: Most clubs are excited to welcome new members, doubts and all!
